english: Mother, how shall I sow the seed? Take the seed out of the bag with your right hand, and throw it. I have thrown it, and the birds are watching us from the tree. Do not fear the birds, daughter. We will cover the seed. When will the grain grow? It will grow when the rain comes. Are you tired? I am not tired. I will sow the whole field.

english: Master, the ears are ripening. Shall we cut them today? We will cut them. Take the blades! The blades are here. Where shall I stand? Stand there by the stone, and I will stand here. And who will bind the wheat? My daughters will bind it with ropes. In the evening we will drink. Are your hands strong? They are strong.

english: Grandmother, black birds are eating our seed! Run and drive them away! Where are your stones? I threw stones, and they came back. Then sit here and sing! They are afraid of songs. Will you sing with me, grandmother? I am old, child. Sing, and I will listen.

english: Be well, woman! Whose field is this? My husband's and my sons'. Be dear to us, guest! The ears are big. Will the year be good? It will be good, if Perkunos does not break the ears. Where are you going? To my brother's house. Eat with us! The road is long.

english: Father, black rain-clouds are coming! Our wheat still lies under the sky. Run to your brothers! Let us quickly carry it into the house! They are carrying it now. english: Friend, sing us the song of the harvest! I will sing it. Sun, ripen our grain! Earth, mother, nourish us! That is sweet. Who taught you? My grandmother taught me, when I was a little girl. Do you know a song? I know the song of the plough. Sing it, guest! We will listen and cut.

english: Master, may I gather the ears which fell? Gather them, girl. Whose daughter are you? I am the daughter of a widow. My mother has no wealth. Then take grain from my heap. Bring it to her. You are good, master. May the gods give you good things.

english: Grandmother, where shall I sow the barley? In the wet field. Barley loves water. And the wheat? Put it on the hill; wheat loves the sun. Did your father not teach you? He did not teach me. He died last year. Then I will teach you, young man. Come in the morning.

english: Brother, how many bags are full? Ten bags are full. The others are half full. Will we be hungry in winter? We will not be hungry. Last year the grain was greater. Did you give grain to our mother? I gave her two full bags. She nourishes the whole household.

english: Mother-in-law, the millstones are heavy. I have grown tired. Grind, daughter-in-law! Whoever sits does not eat. You are sitting too! I sit and grind wheat. Show me your flour! This is my flour. Is it clean? It is clean. Shall we cook bread for your husband? Let us cook it.

english: Grandmother, tell me the story of the rain. The rivers were dry, and men were hungry. What did they do? They prayed for rain. Perkunos heard the men from the sky. Did he give rain? He hit the cloud with his stone, and it rained on all the fields. You ask him, child! Do you tremble before Perkunos? I do not tremble.

english: Father, shall I plough today? You are small, daughter. The plough is heavy. I am strong! Yesterday I carried water from the river. Then lead the oxen. Sing to them; they hear well. english: Mistress, what are you carrying in the pot? Barley mush and beer. Sit down and fill yourselves! We are thirsty, and the sun is warm. How many fields did you cut today? We cut three fields. Two remain. Then drink beer, and cut them in the morning!

english: Mother, I am hungry. Is the bread cooking? It is cooking on the stones. Wait, son. I smell it. Give me a little! Bring wood for the fire! Then I will give you bread. I carried the wood. Now give me bread! Eat! Leave the rest for your father. Is it sweet? It is sweet!

english: Wife, where shall we hide the grain from the mice? Dig beside the house, and put the pots there. Will the mice not find the grain there? We will cover the pots with a stone. english: Friend, is your plough new? It is new. I hewed it myself from wood. Its furrows are straight. My oxen are strong. They pull it. Do you have cattle? I have an old cow. Then lead my oxen in the morning and plough! You are dear to me!
